The round has two phases. In the retrospective phase participants retrieve hits from an affinity selection mass spectrometry screen of 400,000 compounds, seeking the most diverse set of hidden hits; the top ten are then invited to predict novel hits prospectively from the Enamine catalogue, which the organisers procure and test experimentally at their own cost. This is the design that separates it from a retrospective benchmark: the number a participant is judged on is produced by an experiment that happens after the prediction. The record did not submit a prediction and did not see the experimental results.

name: Beyond Random Splits
summary: Study of drug-target affinity prediction under chemically and biologically motivated distribution shifts, which finds that the agreement between architectures falls from 0.79 under two chemical shifts to 0.39 under a protein shift and reverses to -0.55 under a shift that combines them.

identifiers.value: Beyond Random Splits: Evaluating Drug-Target Affinity Models Under Chemically and Biologically Motivated Distribution Shifts; Chung, Li, Muthukumaran, Wang, Iyer, Tan, Sathu, Nnamdi, Tamo, Marteau and Wang, arXiv 2610.03456, submitted 2 October 2026

evidence.label: The arXiv record of the paper, read on 2026-10-24, with its title, author list, submission date and abstract

caveats: The arXiv page states no released repository, processed dataset or code location, so the record carries no licence and no established access level. The underlying sources it names are ChEMBL and BindingDB, which have their own terms.

The study curates 718,800 unique drug-protein pairs and compares a Morgan-fingerprint and protein-CNN baseline with twelve further architectures built from four drug representations and three ESM-2 interaction modes, which is a large comparison rather than a small one.

The reported validation RMSE is 0.950 for the scaffold shift and 0.945 for the fingerprint-cluster shift, against 1.299 for the protein-cluster shift and 1.321 for the dual shift, so the error rises under the biological shifts while the ranking behaviour changes far more sharply: the architectures agree at a rank correlation of 0.79 under the two chemical shifts, at 0.39 under the protein shift, and at -0.55 under the dual shift, where the order reverses.

The paper's own conclusion is that the model choice depends on the extrapolation setting rather than on the average error or on the quantity of training data, and it says that a drug-target affinity benchmark should reproduce the chemical and target shifts expected in deployment. The record did not run the comparison.
